name: STS40 high-accuracy temperature sensor
description: Sensirion STS4x 16-bit digital temperature sensor (-40 to 125 °C, ±0.2 °C typical, 0.01 °C resolution) with an I2C interface and CRC-checked readings at fixed address 0x44 (STS40-AD1B). The chip runs on 1.08–3.6 V. Sold as: MikroElektronika Thermo 24 Click (MIKROE-5110), a mikroBUS board with two 8-pin headers (AN, RST, CS, SCK, MISO, MOSI, 3V3, GND / PWM, INT, RX, TX, SCL, SDA, 5V, GND; only 3V3, GND, SCL and SDA are needed), a PCA9306 I2C level translator with a VIO SEL jumper (3V3 default / 5V) and a power LED.
eli5: A very precise thermometer that tells your board the temperature to a fifth of a degree.

buildNotes: Wire it with jumper leads: only 3V3, GND, SCL and SDA are needed. Leave the VIO SEL jumper in its default left (3V3) position for an ESP32, Pico or Raspberry Pi.
Power the sensor from 3.3 V only: the STS40 is rated 1.08–3.6 V and the board has no regulator on the 3V3 pin.
Single-shot high-precision command is one byte, 0xFD; wait at least 8.3 ms (10 ms is safe) before reading 3 bytes: temperature MSB, LSB, CRC.
Check the CRC (poly 0x31, init 0xFF; 0xBEEF gives 0x92). A mismatch almost always means a loose SDA/SCL wire.
The address is fixed at 0x44 in the chip (STS40-AD1B), so only one Thermo 24 Click per I2C bus.
Keep the sensor away from the power LED, regulator and microcontroller, which warm the air around them.

driver.code:
# STS40 high-accuracy temperature sensor (Sensirion STS4x), MicroPython driver.
# Single-shot measurement: write one command byte, wait for the conversion, read 3 bytes
# (T MSB, T LSB, CRC-8 poly 0x31 init 0xFF). T = -45 + 175 * S / 65535 degC (datasheet eq. 1).
# Commands: 0xFD high (max 8.3 ms), 0xF6 medium (max 4.5 ms), 0xE0 low (max 1.6 ms) repeatability,
# 0x89 serial number, 0x94 soft reset (max 1 ms).
import time


def _crc8(data):
    crc = 0xFF
    for b in data:
        crc ^= b
        for _ in range(8):
            crc = ((crc << 1) ^ 0x31) & 0xFF if crc & 0x80 else (crc << 1) & 0xFF
    return crc


_MODES = {'high': (0xFD, 10), 'medium': (0xF6, 5), 'low': (0xE0, 2)}


class STS40:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x44):
        # STS40-AD1B answers at 0x44 (BD1B: 0x45, CD1B: 0x46). The address is fixed in the chip.
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        time.sleep_ms(1)  # power-up time tPU is at most 1 ms

    def reset(self):
        """Soft reset (0x94); the sensor is idle again after at most 1 ms."""
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, b'\x94')
        time.sleep_ms(1)

    def serial_number(self):
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, b'\x89')
        time.sleep_ms(1)
        d = self.i2c.readfrom(self.addr, 6)
        if _crc8(d[0:2]) != d[2] or _crc8(d[3:5]) != d[5]:
            raise OSError('STS40 CRC mismatch: check the wiring')
        return (d[0] << 24) | (d[1] << 16) | (d[3] << 8) | d[4]

    def read_raw(self, mode='high'):
        cmd, wait_ms = _MODES[mode]
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes([cmd]))
        time.sleep_ms(wait_ms)
        d = self.i2c.readfrom(self.addr, 3)
        if _crc8(d[0:2]) != d[2]:
            raise OSError('STS40 CRC mismatch: check the wiring')
        return (d[0] << 8) | d[1]

    def temperature(self, mode='high'):
        """Measure once and return the temperature in degrees C."""
        return -45 + 175 * self.read_raw(mode) / 65535

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from sts40 import STS40

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
sensor = STS40(i2c)
while True:
    print('T=%.2fC' % sensor.temperature())
    time.sleep(1)
